enclosure-mounting-hardware.description: Enclosure mounting hardware, per rfc/rfcs/2026-08-14-enclosure-mounting-hardware.md (merged as rfc#17, then narrowed by Seve). Adds <enclosure.fdm.heatsetinsert>, <assembly.bolt|screw|screen|cable>, removes <enclosure.screwboss> and the <hole selfTapping> prop. The load-bearing idea: the fastening method is carried by WHICH ELEMENT IS PRESENT, not by a flag -- a screw threads into the plastic, a bolt threads into an insert -- so no prop can contradict the hardware, and the bore that gets cut (self-tap pilot vs insert install diameter) follows from the element. props and core are done and green; the whole remainder is create-fdm-enclosure, whose branch is cut but empty.
enclosure-mounting-hardware.$order: props must land before core: core's components import assemblyScrewProps and the fastenerGeometry helpers. create-fdm-enclosure consumes both.
enclosure-mounting-hardware.$remaining: In create-fdm-enclosure: (1) EnclosureMountInput gains threadEngagement, pilotDiameter, bottomClearance, boreEntryChamfer; (2) getRequiredEngagementMm honours the authored value, default 2.5x nominal, up from a hardcoded 2x; (3) getMountBoreDiameterMm honours the authored pilot, default 0.8x nominal, replacing the per-thread catalogue constant; (4) getMountBossDiameterMm calls props' getBossOuterDiameterMm, one max() instead of a branch per fastening; (5) insertMeltReliefMm and selfTapPilotReliefMm are DELETED, both call sites reading the converged bottomClearance; (6) a 45-degree chamfer cone subtracted at the bore mouth. Expect the enclosure fixtures to need rewriting: an M3 self-tapping mount goes from 6+1mm of boss depth to 7.5+3mm, so existing standoffs stop fitting.
enclosure-mounting-hardware.$deferred: Boss support: whether a boss is merged into a side wall (enough support) or freestanding (needs gussets or ribs). Deliberately out of scope -- a boss today has no knowledge of walls at all, so this needs new geometry and its own design pass.
enclosure-mounting-hardware.$consumers: 3d-viewer, circuit-json-to-gltf and modelprinter render the hardware and are NOT patched here; that is the next phase. They are rebuilt from workspace.json's bundling graph (`./tsc-dev rebuild --from core`).

enclosure-mounting-hardware.description: Three sibling layers -- a Git base has to live in the same repository, so none bases on another -- but they must MERGE in order: props, then core, then create-fdm-enclosure. Not ready to publish: the solver layer is an empty branch.
